written: 2026-11-19, while s6-comp trained, before the execution-MBR diagnostic or the MBR methods ran on any evaluation set; the only earlier run was a 12-task smoke test on held-out teacher tasks to check the code (first verified 5, MBR 4, oracle 6), and a 2-task smoke test on training tasks
motivation: On held-out teacher tasks, s5-var's first verified program is correct for 52 tasks at beam width 32 and 57 at width 128, while some verified program is correct for 65 and 86 (reports/seedlm/discovery3_s5-var.json): a selection gap that grows with the beam. The consensus round found that agreement on fresh inputs is evidence of correctness (docs/consensus.md)
hypothesis: Among the coder's verified programs, the behaviour carrying the most beam probability on probe inputs (execution minimum Bayes risk) is correct more often than the most probable program
method: mylittlellm/seedlm/select.py as of commit 3132898: 24 probe inputs from the consensus probe grammar (type-preserving mutations of the visible example's arguments), each program run with a 0.1 s limit, two programs agree when at least 3 probes give both a value and none differ, a program's support is its own beam probability plus that of every program agreeing with it, ties keep beam order. Nothing here is tuned on any evaluation set
coder: the adopted coder when the measures run (s5-var unless a SeedLM-6 arm is adopted first)
primary_measure: held-out teacher tasks (139), scripts/seedlm7_mbr.py: tasks whose MBR-chosen program is correct on all three cases, against the first verified program, at widths 32 and 128. Supported if MBR solves at least 5 more than the first program at width 128 and no fewer at width 32; not supported if it solves fewer at either width; inconclusive otherwise
secondary_measures: the same on the held-out engine failures with a teacher one-liner (15), counts only
on the held-out development fifth (scripts/seedlm4_tasks.py holdout --mbr): pyx_mbr against pyx_model, and pyx_override_mbr against pyx_override, with fixes and breaks against the engine
choice: an MBR method replaces the adopted method only if it solves more of the held-out development fifth than the adopted coder's best (69 for s5-var); then the validation gate (alone no fewer than the engine's 19 of 45; in the 1.5B pipeline no fewer than 31), one MBPP+ test run and one HumanEval+ run

outcome.written: 2026-11-19, after the pre-registered measures on s5-var
outcome.primary: held-out teacher tasks: MBR 48 vs first 52 at width 32 (15 picks changed), 52 vs 57 at width 128 (28 changed); oracle 65 and 86. MBR solves fewer at both widths: not supported (reports/seedlm/mbr_s5-var.json)

secondary.held_out_development: pyx_mbr 58 vs pyx_model 57 (fixes/breaks against the engine 5/12 vs 5/13); pyx_override_mbr 69 vs pyx_override 69; the eight earlier methods reproduce s5-var's earlier run exactly (reports/seedlm/holdout4_s5-var_mbr.json)

outcome.choice: best method 69, not more than 69: nothing replaced
outcome.reading: Programs in one coder's beam share its mistakes: wrong programs come as families of near-equivalent variants that agree on probes and pool their probability, while a correct program is often alone. Agreement is evidence only between sources whose errors are independent (docs/consensus.md); within a beam it measures the coder's own bias
